impact_summary: GitLab.com was degraded beginning around 19:00 UTC on January 31st, with many users unable to post comments on issues and merge requests while load was brought under control. Database changes made between January 31st 17:20 UTC and 23:30 UTC were permanently lost, including at least 5000 projects, 5000 comments, and roughly 700 users, affecting only GitLab.com users. Recovery from the outage was not completed until around 18:00 UTC on February 1st, roughly 24 hours later, after an approximately 18-hour data copy.

action_items.action: Enable WAL archiving on the production PostgreSQL primary so that replicas can catch up after falling behind, rather than requiring a manual re-synchronisation.
Verify backups by performing regular automated restore tests of pg_dump and LVM/disk-based backups into an isolated environment, and alert on restore failures.
Fix the pg_dump version selection so backup jobs on application servers use the PostgreSQL 9.6 client binaries matching the production database, and fail loudly if the versions mismatch.
Enable DMARC alignment for cronjob notification emails and add an independent alerting path (such as a dead-man's-switch check on backup completion) so backup failures cannot go unnoticed.

Require explicit host identity confirmation (such as hostname checks or a confirmation prompt showing the target role) before running destructive operations on database data directories, and restrict such commands to documented runbooks.
Document in engineering runbooks that pg_basebackup waits silently for the primary to begin streaming, and add expected-output and timeout guidance for this step.

Review and correct PostgreSQL configuration on the primary, lowering max_connections from an unreasonable value and sizing max_wal_senders appropriately, and add configuration review checks to detect out-of-range settings.
Enable Azure disk snapshots for database servers, and document expected restore times for snapshots across storage accounts.
Establish a defined incident response process with a designated incident commander and a coordination channel, so responders do not rely on informal Slack requests to locate backups during an outage.
Evaluate deploying a multi-replica database topology with a dedicated read-capable standby and connection pooling to reduce single-primary load and single point of failure risk.
Investigate the background user-removal job so that accidental or flagged account deletions are soft-deleted and rate-limited rather than hard-deleted in bulk.
Require ad hoc production-to-staging snapshots to follow a documented, reviewed procedure, and restrict load testing on staging environments that may affect production risk.
Provision premium or faster storage for staging database hosts used in restore procedures, or document restore time expectations based on current storage throughput.
